message: Constellation Challenge 2023 cover for Arezzo&Co by Argos Capital.
layout_trick: Left dark panel with big bold white title and a diagonal cyan swoosh over a full-bleed store photo; company logo bottom-right, team names bottom-left.

message: Brazil's footwear market is more mature than the world's but apparel is still recovering, and a heavily clustered A/B consumer base drives spending.
layout_trick: Left callout box with a value-chain icon stack (design, manufacturing, distribution) beside 4 compact charts, each with a one-line bold takeaway above it.

message: Brazilian apparel and footwear are fragmented but consolidating via M&A, with Arezzo&Co at 25% of women's footwear share.
layout_trick: Logo wall of acquired brands in a shaded box next to a market-share donut and a share-evolution line chart, tying consolidation text to visuals.

message: Arezzo&Co and Soma lead on pricing power and diversified channel mix, so they are more resilient in downturns.
layout_trick: Peer logos on rows with horizontal dots on a C- to A+ customer-class scale, plus a smooth line chart of inflation vs revenue variation with an annotation callout.

message: International brands struggle in Brazil due to import tariffs and taxes, and Shein is the one growing as a low-price threat.
layout_trick: Logo timeline by entry decade across the top, with Shein vs Arezzo comparison logos and price-benchmark bars below.

message: E-commerce accelerated by the pandemic and is the future, but Brazil's penetration is still well below other regions.
layout_trick: Three stacked chart bands (columns with CAGR badge, benchmark bars highlighting Brazil in cyan, ribbon of yearly values) all in the same dark-grey and cyan palette.

message: Omnichannel and influencers are the key digital opportunity for apparel and footwear brands.
layout_trick: Right-hand cyan-tinted panel isolates the influencer sub-story (histogram, donut, takeaway box) from the left channel-penetration charts.

message: Men's apparel is a fragmented, higher-ticket gold mine and the best consolidation opportunity.
layout_trick: Men vs women shown consistently as dark vs cyan series across line, stacked 100% bars and paired columns, so the gender contrast reads at a glance.

message: Casualization and sustainability are lasting trends, but price is still the decisive factor for buyers.
layout_trick: Row of five small donuts with one-line labels for decisive purchase factors, beneath a Google Trends line with a dark callout stat box.

message: Four main risks (destructive competition, bad tax reform, high rates, global recession) are mapped by probability x impact, with Shein and SELIC as the biggest.
layout_trick: Risk matrix with impact vs probability grid and named cells placed in the grid, paired on the right with evidence charts for each risk (SELIC line, Shein users, ICMS bars).
